title: Swift Stallbreaker: Rapid Deal Acceleration Deck (Proto)
content:
Summary:
A compact slide deck (8–12 slides) for SEs + RMs to remove late-stage stalls during pilot and procurement. Focus: 10-minute play checks, a technical 'quick-handoff' for platform/infra concerns, procurement talking points (cost predictability + reserved models), and an emergency fallback script when security/legal asks for air-gapped options.

Structure / Slide-by-slide (speaker notes + bullets):
1) Cover + TL;DR (slide)
- Title: Swift Stallbreaker
- One-line: Short checklist to convert a stalled pilot into a signed POC or reserved commitment within 30 days.
- Speak: "This is the 10-minute runbook we hand to an SE when a pilot goes quiet or procurement raises an objection."

2) Common stall patterns (slide)
- Bullets: Procurement price shock; security review (data residency/KMS/HSM); performance worries (latency at scale); feature mismatch (tool-calling, streaming); unclear success metrics.
- Speak: "Map the stall to one of these patterns quickly — it dictates our play."

3) Quick triage checklist (slide + one-pager insert)
- 3-question triage: Who is blocking? (procurement/security/tech/exec) | What is the timeline? | What is the required deliverable to move forward?
- Actionable: Assign owner, set 48-hr sprint, propose 1 concrete deliverable (benchmarked latency report, compliance checklist, demo env).

4) Tech rapid-handoff (slide)
- Fast items SEs can trigger in 24–72h: ephemeral demo VPC, small Dedicated tranche (2–4 GPUs) for baseline SLA, run a 1-hour latency/cost simulation with the customer's prompt set.
- Speaker tip: "Offer to run the customer's top 10 queries on a 2-GPU reserved node and share token-level latency/cost — customers pay attention to real numbers."

5) Procurement scripts (slide)
- Option framing: Hosted trial -> Reserved pilot -> Annual reserved commit.
- Cost arguments: predictable per-hour committed capacity vs burst; expected token economics with caching; billing clarity (per-token + reserved baseline).
- Template line: "If you want predictability, we can lock a dedicated pool for X months and cap unit spend with weekly reports."

6) Security counter-checks & evidence pack (slide)
- Checklist: SOC2 status, KMS integration notes, optional private control plane, audit log samples, sample SLA language.
- Attachments to send: security one-pager, architecture diagram with VPC peering option, sample ATO checklist.

7) Field-ready objection zingers (one-slide cheat sheet)
- Objection: "What about model drift / regressions?" -> Answer: "We run your eval suite during rollouts, rollback policies, and quality alerts for top prompts."
- Objection: "We need air-gapped" -> Answer: "We provide a Private package and an on-prem installer; share requirements and we scope."
- Objection: "Too expensive at scale" -> Answer: "We’ll show two paths: quantized model + caching for cost-first, or dedicated throughput for latency-first. We’ll baseline both."

8) 48-hour priority action plan (slide)
- Day 0–1: Triage call + assign owner + schedule demo on dedicated node
- Day 2: Deliver latency/cost cheat sheet, security packet, and optional procurement template
- Day 3–7: Quick follow-ups, legal redlines, pilot acceptance criteria written up

9) Email templates & Slack snippets (appendix slide)
- Short email to procurement: 3-paragraph template offering a dedicated node trial and a cost cap.
- Slack DM to SE team: checklist to request infra, contact SRE: "Please provision 2xA10G-dev for 48 hours for pilot xyz" (replace A10G with customer-preferred GPU).

10) Metrics to share (slide)
- Must-share: 95th pct token latency, avg cost per 1k tokens (hosted vs committed), cache hit rate, tokens saved via prefix caching.
- Present as: single-row table + one-sentence interpretation for non-technical buyers.

Appendix: Examples / Templates / Open questions
- Example: "Dedicated trial outcome" one-pager (mini-case): fintech customer reduced avg latency from 420ms -> 85ms and saw 32% cost drop after prefix caching and 8-bit quantization. (fabricated example for illustration).
- Attach template procurement clause: "Reserved capacity shall be billed monthly; overages billed at X% above committed rate; emergency fallback to hosted models allowed with 48-hr notice."
- Open Qs (to solve before finalizing): who owns small-burst GPU budget for SE-driven demos? Can we auto-provision a 48-hr dedicated on demand? Need SRE playbook for emergency provisioning.

Delivery notes (how to use this deck)
- Use in a live triage with customer + internal stakeholders. Keep deck lightweight: hand the one-pager and the email templates, avoid >12 slides in customer-facing version.
- Goal: move stalled pilot to a concrete next step (dedicated trial, signed POC scope, or legal acceptance).

Action items before next review:
- [Ethan] Wire up a canned demo image for 2xA10G reserved trial (deadline: 2024-12-06).
- [Lena] Draft security one-pager and sample audit logs (deadline: 2024-11-22).
- [Marcus] Build a 10-query benchmarking script that outputs token-level latency + cost (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/field-kits/pull/42).
- [Aisha] Iterate deck copy and produce a customer-facing 6-slide summary.

Notes to self / rough language fragments:
- "If speed to decision is the ask, we'll buy the first week of compute to demonstrate the economics. We eat that cost under $X if it closes in 30 days."
- "Procurement cares about predictability — tie the committed pool number to an easy visual (thermometer chart)."
- "Always ask for prompt sets before demos — synthetic prompts mislead."

References / Related artifacts:
- Internal demo recording: internal:demo-recording-2024-11-08
- Playbook draft: confluence://GTMS/rapid-stall-breaker-notes
- Jira ticket for provisioning automation: JIRA-GTMS-9123

Status: draft — this is intentionally lean. Want to test with two SEs in Dec and iterate based on friction logs.

Unresolved: who is primary budget approver for ad-hoc demos? recommend: field engineering budget line for pilot facilitation.

End of proto deck notes.
